Thursday 25 June 2026 at 20:00 UTC. Ecuador and Germany on the card. On the Ecuador side, the engine's number sits +8.1pp clear of the market — a substantive gap this far out from kickoff.

On Elo, Germany comes in 110 points ahead — Ecuador at 1790, Germany at 1900. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 27%, the draw at 23%, and Germany to win at 50%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Ecuador sits at 27% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Ecuador to win at 18%, the draw at 24%, and Germany to win at 56%. On the Ecuador side specifically the market reads 18%, which prices out at American odds of +441. Compared against the model's 27%, that's the +8.1pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Ecuador the lower bound is 23%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +4.0pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Ecuador priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 30 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
